name: Sven's Camp
summary: In Duskwood, Sven Yorgen's grief still drives him to seek answers about his family's slaughter. A buried journal at the ruined farm may reveal who witnessed it.

sections.title: A Clue in the Dirt
sections.body: Sven Yorgen returned to find his family dead and his farm in ruins after dark riders struck while he was away. Grief and vengeance drove him to send allies to search the wreckage of the homestead. Beneath a mound of freshly turned earth lay a small, dirt-stained book, hastily hidden by a shadowy figure.

sections.title: A Silent Witness
sections.body: At his camp in the western hills, Sven learns what the book contains. The journal proves that a shadowy figure watched the massacre of his family. Instead of bringing peace, it turns Sven toward finding the unknown onlooker and demanding answers.

faq.q: What is the book found in the mound of dirt?
faq.answer: The book is a small, untitled, dirt-stained journal buried at the Yorgen farm. Its entries prove an unidentified onlooker watched the massacre of Sven Yorgen's family.

faq.q: Where does this quest lead next?
faq.answer: Delivering the book to Sven Yorgen sets off a search for the mysterious witness and leads into The Shadowy Figure.

aliases: where do i turn this in
faq.answer: Sven has taken refuge in a camp in Duskwood's northwestern hills, grieving his family's fate and plotting retribution.

faq.q: Why was the book buried at the farm?
faq.answer: The book lay hidden in loose dirt amid the ruined homestead. It may have been hastily discarded or concealed by the observer who lingered at the scene of the attack.
Dark riders from Deadwind Pass slaughtered Sven's family while he was away from the farm.

faq.q: What faction can complete this quest?
faq.answer: Only Alliance players can complete it; Sven Yorgen seeks aid from the defenders of Duskwood and the Alliance.

angles.text: As an Alliance member, you can help investigate the Yorgen massacre as the Alliance struggles to understand the dark forces encroaching on Duskwood.
